active_notes.reason: Played for England to the 2026 World Cup semifinal (lost July 15, 2026); confirmed not returning to Arsenal training until Aug 10, only 11 days before the Aug 21 season opener, while also managing a pre-existing hamstring nerve issue. Source: Arsenal/England reporting, mid-to-late July 2026.

Played for England to the 2026 World Cup semifinal (lost July 15, 2026), reportedly playing through Achilles pain for much of the tournament per manager Thomas Tuchel; confirmed not returning to Arsenal training until Aug 10, only 11 days before the Aug 21 season opener. Source: Arsenal/England reporting, mid-to-late July 2026.

Suffered a fifth metatarsal fracture during pre-season training in Austria (late July 2026), underwent surgery; multiple independent sources (Yahoo Sports, Get French Football News, VAVEL, Sports Mole) consistently report a 3-4 month layoff. Scored 13 goals in 33 appearances last season, so a real, widely-owned FPL asset (~185k estimated owners), not a fringe player -- genuinely misses a significant chunk of the season, not just early-season sharpness. Source: multiple outlets, late July/early August 2026.

Started England's 2026 World Cup semifinal loss to Argentina (July 15, 2026), then completed a brand-new 157.2m transfer from Aston Villa to Chelsea during the tournament window -- so faces BOTH World Cup recovery AND integrating into a new club/system simultaneously. Real, sourced positive signal: has already done one individual training session at Cobham (ahead of Rice/Saka's fully-absent status), but is not expected to join the full Chelsea squad until their pre-season tour concludes ~Aug 9, with a possible debut in the final pre-season friendly Aug 15 -- just 6 days before the Aug 21 opener. Severity set slightly lower than Rice/Saka given the earlier partial return, but genuine risk remains given the new-club integration on top of World Cup fatigue. Source: RotoWire, OneFootball, multiple outlets, early August 2026.

Played the full 120 minutes of England's World Cup quarterfinal vs Norway while managing a hamstring issue during the tournament, then featured in the semifinal loss to Argentina (July 15, 2026) -- heavy accumulated minutes on a carried injury, same knockout-run length as Rice/Saka. Source: Sky Sports, ESPN, mid-July 2026.

Played in the actual 2026 World Cup FINAL for Argentina (lost 1-0 to Spain, July 19, 2026) -- came on for Julian Alvarez in extra time and went the full remaining distance to the final whistle (~120 minutes). This is the single longest possible tournament run of any player in this squad (one match later than the semifinalists), so the return-to-club-training window is correspondingly the latest. Source: Yahoo News, Wikipedia, World Soccer Talk, July 2026.

Played 150 real minutes across France's 2026 World Cup run (lost semifinal to Spain, July 14), including coming on for the injured William Saliba in the 30th minute of the semifinal itself -- genuine tournament minutes, but as a squad-depth/injury-replacement option rather than a full-tournament nailed starter, so a milder discount than the heaviest-minutes cases (Rice/Saka/Guehi/Senesi). Source: CPFC.co.uk, Toffeeweb, July 2026.

Forced off with a right leg injury in Brighton's pre-season friendly win over Roma after a tangle with Bryan Cristante, following lengthy on-field treatment. Brighton expect him to be out 2-3 months; unclear at this stage whether surgery will be required. Compounds an already-depleted Brighton attack (first-choice winger Kaoru Mitoma also out with a hamstring issue). Source: Sussex Express, OneFootball, VAVEL, TribalFootball -- mid-August 2026.

17-year-old forward injured on his competitive debut in the UEFA Super Cup defeat to PSG (scoring Villa's goal, becoming the youngest scorer in that competition's history, before being sidelined). Confirmed out for the season opener vs Brighton plus Villa's fixtures against Arsenal, Hull City, Nottingham Forest, and Tottenham (Sept 19) -- some reports suggest a 6-week timeline. Had starred throughout pre-season prior to the injury. Source: LiveScore, Yahoo Sports, Goal.com, Read Aston Villa -- mid-August 2026.

Confirmed as Brighton's main penalty taker and primary corner/free-kick taker for 2026-27, per Premier League Scout coverage: now handling penalty duties and main taker of corners and free-kicks. Cross-verified via multiple independent set-piece-duty trackers (RotoWire, xFPL, FPL Pilot) covering the season. Source: Premier League Scout, RotoWire, xFPL, August 2026.

Confirmed as Brentford's first-choice penalty taker for 2026-27, retaining the role after a 22-goal Premier League season last year. Multiple independent set-piece-duty trackers (RotoWire, xFPL, FPL Pilot, allaboutfpl) agree he keeps penalty duties, not handed off to a new signing. Source: RotoWire (Premier League Set-Piece Takers 2026/27), August 2026.

Established as Liverpool's primary free-kick taker under Arne Slot -- real, confirmed track record (104 corners, 38 free kicks, 78 chances created last season per set-piece trackers). Penalty and corner duties are LESS certain following Mohamed Salah's departure: reporting describes him as a contender who 'could be on everything,' not a confirmed penalty taker -- the decision may not be made until Liverpool's first penalty of the season. Severity set modestly to reflect the confirmed free-kick role without overstating the still-undecided penalty/corner picture. Source: RotoWire (Premier League Set-Piece Takers 2026/27), Liverpoolfc.com, Full90 FPL -- August 2026.
